This would need a legal entity. I'm thinking this would probably be a 501(c)(3) (non-profit corporation). There is overhead involved in running it (filing forms, governance).

https://www.councilofnonprofits.org/tools-resources/how-start-nonprofit

The corporation needs to be filed in some state. I've heard that Delaware is one of the best places to form corporations (at least for-profit, I'm not sure about non-profit).

Some reasons why a legal entity is needed:

- Banks / payment processors / web hosts generally need to know who they're doing business with (whether an individual or a corporation).

- Legal protection (lawsuits target the corporation, not you personally)

- Tax protection. (If you, as an individual, receive money - it is taxable income. Even if you're spending it on a good cause).

- Cryptocurrency is also taxable, and a bit harder to work with as far as tax goes (than dealing with cash/check/credit card contributions). Per IRS regulations, value of the crypto at the time you buy (receive) vs sell counts as capital gains (or losses).

- Note: non-profit corporations still need to follow GAAP.

IRS has some resources. https://www.stayexempt.irs.gov/home/resource-library/virtual-small-mid-size-tax-exempt-organization-workshop

What you can't (shouldn't) do is put up a web site and receive money before a legal foundation is in place. Once that's done, raising funds can be done flexibly.
